messages:
leigh: Quick flag 1: dropped canary alert: one ingress node presented a cert whose issuer doesn't match our keystore alias for prod-keystore. Small blast radius but reproducible.
ux-ops: where's the evidence? sample logs or fingerprint?
kms-sentinel-bot: ALERT: KMS Unwrap anomaly detected for key=prod-keystore at 2026-11-03T18:12Z. unwrap_principal=serviceAccount:deploy-runner@infra.example.com; signer_fingerprint=4f:2a:99 (expected 9c:7b:11). Shadow cert auto-created for ingress-canary.
leigh: fingerprint 4f:2a:99 is not in our CA inventory. Did we recently grant any temp IAM bindings to infra service accounts?
tan: checking IAM change history now. I see a terraform apply on 2026-11-02T22:01Z that created a binding with note "crossproj-keystore-test". Creator=ci-bot@infra.example.com.
rory: grep KMS audit: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName:("AsymmetricUnwrapKey" OR "Decrypt") AND resource.labels.key_id="prod-keystore" AND timestamp>="2026-11-02T21:00:00Z"' --limit 50` shows unwraps at 18:10Z by deploy-runner and a Decrypt at 18:11Z by serviceAccount:external-sync@partner.example.com.
oncall-elena: external-sync@partner? that's unexpected. Did we set up any partner replication recently?
tan: infra claims a staged replication feature was toggled for a pilot. I'll ask infra who approved the terraform apply.
rory: mitigation checklist I recommend: 1) revoke the test binding immediately 2) mark the key to extended audit retention 3) rotate certs that used the suspect unwrap 4) add an org-policy deny to prevent non-org principals from binding to prod keystore keys 5) start provenance sweep for other keys. Assign tan + leigh.
leigh: revoking now: `gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding projects/.../keys/prod-keystore --member="serviceAccount:ci-bot@infra.example.com" --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"` 1: revoke logged.
kms-sentinel-bot: NOTE: shadow certs are staged for ingress; auto-promotion disabled pending manual review.
oncall-elena: I'll take incident lead if we confirm external decrypts. Legal on standby. Keep severity S2 for now.
tan: infra responds: the terraform run was approved in the UI by user=ops-admin@infra.example.com. Approval metadata shows ip=198.51.100.22. Need to confirm that click was from internal SSO and not delegated.
rory: I pulled egress flow logs for the rotator pod around 18:08-18:15Z: outbound to acme-relay.certs.example-cdn.net (52.210.10.40) with UA acme-client/2.3. That looks normal for ACME interactions. The odd part is the external-sync principal in KMS decrypts.
leigh: possible causes: pipeline targeted wrong project, partner principal accidentally granted via group mapping, or token leak. Prioritize proving whether external principal caused any production cert to be served.
tan: proxy logs indicate only a single canary node served the 4f:2a:99 cert. We rolled that node to the shadow cert and handshake errors stopped. No customer-facing impact so far.
rory: Forensics tasks: export all KMS unwrap/decrypt events for prod-keystore last 90d, join with terraform audit changes, and collect approval click metadata for any terraform runs that touched kms bindings. I'll push results to sec-bq.
oncall-elena: temporary controls: 1) block partner identities from approving infra changes to prod via org-policy 2) require 2 human approvers for any terraform resource touching kms keys 3) rotate pipeline tokens used in the timeframe.
kms-sentinel-bot: INFO: no CT/ocsp entries found for fingerprint 4f:2a:99 in public logs in last 180 days.
leigh: good. if CT shows nothing we likely prevented a widespread leakage. Still close the process gap. Add to vuln-triage and label as "keystore-binding-process-gap".
tan: infra will patch the pipeline to reject applies that target prod keystore without an EXPLICIT_PROD_CONFIRM flag and will log approver metadata to secure storage. ETA: next deploy window.
rory: I'll add canonical scripts to correlate unwrap->csr->certserial and make a dashboard alert if any unwraps are performed by non-org principals.
oncall-elena: legal & trust ops notified. If more external principals show up escalate to P1. For now keep watch through the 72-hour audit window.
leigh: thanks team. Keep updates brief. If you find the origin of 4f:2a:99 outside infra, call it out immediately. :eyes:
